sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Hafgan, also written Havgan, is a Welsh mythological figure. His name means summer song. He was one of two rival kings of the Otherworld who battled constantly. His opponent was Arawn, the better-known king of Annwn. Hafgan carried a magic gift: after he received a second blow, he recovered from any blow. So his opponent had one chance to lay him low. In the Mabinogion, Arawn asked the human prince Pwyll to be his substitute for a year and to fight Hafgan. The two magically swapped their appearances. Arawn ruled Pwyll's land while Pwyll held Arawn's throne in Annwn. At the year's end Pwyll defeated Hafgan in single combat.
objective: Document Hafgan, the rival king defeated by Pwyll in the Mabinogion.
key_results: Record his name Hafgan or Havgan and its meaning summer song.
Describe his rivalry with Arawn of Annwn and his recovery gift.
Retell Pwyll's year-long substitution and single-combat victory.
